To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the institutional arrangements in a locality are important in determining the impact of decentralization on policy.

1) the institutional environment of localities is an important factor that affects economic performance and policy making; 2) local institutions are difficult to change; and 3) the institutional legacy of local center relations can be overcome by increased international economic competition.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
local officials in China have been able to make policy changes that are in their interest, but not in the interest of the central government or of society as a whole.
local institutions are important, and that decentralization may not be a panacea for policy reform.

decentralization may be necessary for policy change but not sufficient, and that the political and institutional environment in which policy is made is a crucial factor in determining whether policy change will be forthcoming.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Chinese auto industry has been a case of policy imitation, where local governments have tried to imitate the institutional arrangements of the most successful localities.
decentralization is a double-edged sword: It may increase the flexibility of policy, but it may also make policy change more difficult.
local officials are more likely to change their policies in response to international competition than to central government pressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
decentralization may improve policy flexibility but the impact on policy change is contingent on local institutions and external competition.
the effects of decentralization on policy making are not immediate and are dependent on the institutional context of a country.
decentralization is not necessarily the best way to achieve economic policy reform.
